what_it_does: Quantum computers make frequent errors because every gate operation has a chance of going wrong; the fewer gates a circuit needs, the less often errors compound. This paper introduces QuCLEAR, a compiler tool that targets a specific class of operations called Clifford gates — operations that can be perfectly simulated on a regular classical computer — and removes them from the quantum hardware workload entirely. It first shuffles Clifford-type gates to the end of the circuit (a process called extraction) while also simplifying the remaining non-Clifford gates that are exposed in the process. Then, because the entire Clifford portion can be computed classically and applied as a mathematical post-correction to the final measurement results, those gates never need to run on the noisy quantum chip at all. The result, based on the abstract, is a meaningful reduction in the number of gates that must execute on error-prone hardware, which should improve the accuracy of near-term quantum computations.
